commit_message:
avformat/mov: don't assume iloc and iinf entries for each item_id will be in the same order

Nothing forbids them to be in any order the muxer desires.

Fixes demuxing heif samples generated by S1II.

Tested-by: Lynne <dev@lynne.ee>
Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>

fix_commit.message: avformat/mov: abort if the queried item doesn't exist instead of overwriting it
fix_commit.author: James Almer

findings.title: mov_read_iloc/mov_read_infe overwrite unrelated HEIF item when queried item_id is never found
findings.suggestion: After the search loop, explicitly check whether the loop ran to completion without finding an empty slot or matching item, i.e. check `if (j == c->nb_heif_item) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;` in addition to the existing `if (!item) return AVERROR(ENOMEM);` check, in both mov_read_iloc and mov_read_infe, before using `item` to store/overwrite fields.

ground_truth.root_cause: The search-or-allocate loop that scans c->heif_item[] for a matching item_id (or an available slot to allocate a new one) does not verify that the loop actually terminated via a `break` (match found or new item allocated) versus falling through the loop's natural end condition. Only a NULL-pointer (allocation failure) check was performed afterward, which is insufficient to detect the 'not found' case where `item` still holds a valid but wrong pointer left over from the last loop iteration.
